title: Short Stuff: Dodleston Messages
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Dodleston Messages (spelled "Doddleston" in parts of the transcript), a 1980s paranormal mystery in England. Ken Webster and his partner Debbie bought an 18th-century cottage (Meadow Cottage) where strange six-toed footprints and stacked cat food cans appeared. Ken later received messages on a BBC Micro running a word processor program called Edward, from an author signing "L" who claimed to be living in 1556 and who was later identified as Thomas (Standford Lucas, or Harden/Hawarden). The hosts discuss logical holes such as the Jesus College, Oxford anachronism, the Jaguar "cart without a horse" reference, and a third party from 2109. An SPR investigation found nothing. Ken Webster's 1989 book The Vertical Plane chronicles the events. The hosts conclude it is most likely a hoax, citing Occam's razor, and note Tom Ruffles' review that considers unconscious telekinesis.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the mystery of the Doddleston Messages, a 1980s occult event in England that inspired a book.

segments.title: Meadow Cottage and early strange events
segments.summary: Ken Webster and Debbie buy an 18th-century cottage. Six-toed footprints appear on the wall and reappear in fresh paint, and cat food cans are stacked in pyramids.

segments.title: BBC Micro and the first message
segments.summary: Ken Webster gets a BBC Micro with the Edward word processor, where messages appear. The author claims to live in 1556. The hosts read the first message and note the computer is not networked and does not save between power-ups.

segments.title: Lucas and early modern English messages
segments.summary: Ken questions the author, who signs as L and is later identified as Lucas. The messages use early modern English, and the pair develop a mutual fondness.

segments.title: Logical holes: Jesus College and the Jaguar
segments.summary: The hosts discuss anachronisms: the author cites Jesus College, Oxford, which was founded in 1571 after his claimed time, and references a picture of Ken's Jaguar car as a cart without a horse.

segments.title: The 2109 third party and the SPR investigation
segments.summary: A third party from 2109 is referenced and then responds, asking to be left alone. The Society for Psychical Research investigates three times and finds no activity. Thomas says he will leave a book for discovery.

segments.title: Hoax verdict
segments.summary: The hosts discuss The Vertical Plane and Tom Ruffles' review, which considers unconscious telekinesis, before concluding the story is most likely a hoax.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the episode and give their final judgment.
